questions.question: What is the name of a constructor?
questions.explanation: Java recognizes a constructor by its class-matching name and lack of return type.

questions.question: What return type is written on a constructor?

options.value: The class name before the method name

questions.explanation: Constructors are not declared with a return type, including void.

questions.question: When does a constructor execute?

options.value: Only after every object is deleted
During creation of a new object

questions.explanation: The constructor initializes the newly allocated object.

questions.question: Can a class define multiple constructors?

options.value: Only if all parameter lists are identical

questions.explanation: Constructor overloading provides different initialization interfaces.

questions.question: When does Java provide an implicit no-argument constructor?

options.value: When the class declares no constructors
Only when all fields are public

questions.explanation: Declaring any constructor prevents the automatic no-argument constructor from being supplied.

questions.question: What is the role of constructor parameters?

options.value: Supply values or choices used to initialize the object
Automatically become fields with the same name

questions.explanation: Parameters are local values that initialization code can copy or process.

questions.question: Which is a constructor in class Ticket?
questions.explanation: The constructor uses the class name and no return type.

questions.question: What should a constructor establish?

options.value: The result of every future method
A static version of all fields

questions.explanation: Later operations can rely on documented initialization and invariants.

questions.question:
What is the field value after new Counter(2)?
public Counter(int start) { count = start + 1; }
questions.explanation: The constructor expression computes start + 1 and stores it.

questions.question:
What is count after new Counter(2, 3)?
public Counter(int first, int second) { count = first + second; }
questions.explanation: Constructor arguments match parameters by position and are added.
